Empires & Puzzles Fosco Review: 4-Star Epic Ice Blue from Masquerade Family

Fosco brings a unique kit of total minion destruction and mass dispelling to the 4-star arena, but does his Slow mana speed leave him stuck in the mud? We analyze if this masked alchemist is worth the tonics or just a potion of disappointment.
Fosco Review: The Slow Motion Minion Melter
Fosco, The Follower of Februus: Potions, Plagues, and Patience

Fosco is a 4-star Epic Ice hero from the Masquerade family, released during the Carnival of Gods event in 2023. He serves as a utility support hero, designed to wipe the board clean of both minions and enemy buffs while providing a steady stream of healing to his allies. While his kit sounds incredible on paper combining two high-value counters into one skill his practical application is heavily defined, and arguably confined, by his Slow mana speed. He is the alchemist who arrives at the party with the cure just as the guests are leaving.

Fosco sports a classic Venetian plague doctor aesthetic, complete with the iconic beaked mask and a colorful, harlequin-patterned hood. He clutches blue potions that look suspiciously like mana potions, though given his speed, he might have forgotten to drink them himself. The art style fits the Carnival of Gods theme perfectly, blending the festive with the slightly ominous.

Fosco's stats are quite respectable for a modern 4-star hero. With a base power of 689, he sits comfortably above the classic Season 1 heroes and even surpasses many older event 4-stars. His stat distribution is fairly balanced, with a slight lean towards bulk (Defense and Health), which is appropriate for a support hero who needs to survive long enough to fire his slow skill. When Limit Broken (LB2), his stats balloon to 848 Attack, 878 Defense, and 1560 Health, making him sturdy enough to survive a few hits in 5-star arenas, though he is primarily built for 4-star tournaments and wars.

He dispels buffs from all enemies. This is arguably his most valuable trait. Full team dispels are premium currency in 4-star rarity, usually reserved for heroes like Sabina or Melendor.
He provides a Heal over Time (HoT) of 540 HP over 3 turns. This translates to 180 HP per turn. It is a decent sustain, but lacks the "save me now" impact of burst healing.

The combination of Minion Destruction and Dispel is rare and powerful. Usually, you have to choose between a dispeller (like Sonya) or a minion killer (like Captain of Diamonds or Gobbler). Fosco does both. However, doing both at Slow speed is his tragic flaw. By the time he charges, the minions may have already done their damage, or the buffs may have already expired.

Fosco is Slow. He requires 12 tiles to charge. With a level 17 mana troop (or equivalent bonuses), you can drop this to 11 tiles, which isn't a significant breakpoint for 3-matches. To get him to 10 tiles, you need a massive 20% mana generation bonus, which is hard to achieve in 4-star restriction environments without specific family bonuses or bards.

Family Bonus, Passives, Aether Power & Unique Abilities
The Masquerade family bonus and passives add layers of survivability that help compensate for his slowness.
The Masquerade family creates a "Mask" minion for the hero at the start of battle or wave. These minions are stat-boosters.

Fosco is immune to Defense Down. This is excellent for a tank or flank, as it ensures he doesn't become squishy due to a Grimm or Tiburtus def-down.
If Fosco's minion dies, he cleanses himself. This creates a funny synergy where if the enemy kills his family minion, he shakes off poisons or silences. It makes him slippery to control.
At the start of battle, he regenerates health for 6 turns. This stacks with his special skill's HoT. It helps him survive the early game tile dump while he tries to charge his slow mana.

If you pull Fosco early, he can be a sturdy tank for your 4-star defense team simply because he is hard to kill. However, do not prioritize him over fast snipers or burst healers (like Kiril or Rigard). He is a tool for specific problems (minions/buffs), not a general-purpose carry.

The community reaction to Fosco was lukewarm at best.
One player noted on the forum:
"I don’t think he will shine in rush battles, damage only equal to minion’s hp... dispel and a low heal over time can do little to help taking down full hp heroes."
Another user humorously pointed out his art:
"Did anyone notice that this guy is Dawa in disguise? Look at the hands."
The general consensus is summarized well by this sentiment:
"At Very Fast, Fosco wouldn’t be broken. He’d be good but still not amazing. At Slow, this is an extremely underpowered hero."
"I will always use C.Gormek over him... Avg speed, damage, minion removal, heal and dispel... vs same skill at slow speed???"

Fosco is a victim of cautious design. In an attempt to not make the "Carnival of Gods" family too overpowered, the developers made their 4-star representative too safe. He does everything you want a utility hero to do destroy minions, dispel buffs, heal but he does it at a pace that feels like he's wading through molasses. He is a beautiful, masked statue: sturdy, artistic, but largely stationary. Keep him for Rush tournaments, but otherwise, let him stay at the carnival.
